player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly assumed that "his" must refer to the employee because feedback is usually given *about* someone else, overlooking the grammatical rule that a pronoun often refers to the closest preceding male noun (the supervisor). In this specific context, "his stellar performance" could logically describe the supervisor's own excellent work, which the employee is being informed about. Next time, I will not rely solely on pragmatic context to resolve ambiguity; instead, I will strictly evaluate if the sentence structure allows for the pronoun to refer to the subject (the supervisor). If both the supervisor and the employee are plausible antecedents without creating a logical contradiction, I will select option (C) Ambiguous rather than forcing a specific antecedent.
